statusDefinitions.supported: The built-in Web renderer implements the fixture's primary rendering and interaction contract. Listed limits are platform adaptations or explicit safety ceilings, not silent no-ops.
statusDefinitions.partial: A functional Web renderer exists, but one or more fixture-backed behaviors or attributes remain unimplemented or intentionally narrower than the native reference.
statusDefinitions.polyfilled: The same observable behaviour as the native reference, built out of different parts - a module web facet with a pinned player, a canvas drawing, a composition over primitives. Under Article 10 a polyfill is a first-class implementation, not a consolation, and a row claiming it must name what implements it.
statusDefinitions.unsupported: A DEFECT, not a resting place (constitution Article 10). No functional Web renderer exists and no polyfill has been shipped, so the DOM runtime renders the unsupported marker. Every such row must carry a matching entry in ClosedSource/release/platform-parity-register.json naming the degradation an author gets today and the polyfill that closes it; check_platform_parity.rb fails otherwise.

universalAttributes._note: The PER-ATTRIBUTE support plane for the catalog universalAttributes (stack-elements.json). Added because the per-element rows above structurally could not record an attribute-level gap: enter/exit/keep/transition/anim/animDuration were silently inert on this renderer for months with no ledger row able to say so. packages/dom/test/attribute-support.test.ts enforces (a) COMPLETENESS — every catalog universal attribute has a row here, and every row names a catalog attribute — and (b) HONESTY for the motion family — a supported motion row must be implemented by element-motion.ts MOTION_HANDLED. A new universal attribute without a row here is a test failure, not a silent gap.

id.reason: Stable id set on the DOM element; ui.node("#id") patches resolve through it.

class.reason: Named styles / DSX-CSS classes applied by wireVisualStyles; later wins.

style.reason: Inline DSX-CSS declarations, static + reactive, via the compiled css handles.

visible-if.reason: Presence anchor + reactive effect; has:scheme answered by the availability seam at mount.

passthrough.reason: Decorative and non-interactive: pointer-events: none on the element and its subtree, the twin of iOS .allowsHitTesting(false) and a Compose Box that does not consume. Implemented late - it shipped on both native renderers and on neither the web nor the census, so a scrim over a tappable video ate every touch here and the linter called the real word a typo.

container.reason: ResizeObserver publishes live width/height as dsx.element.* to descendants.

measure.reason: Writes the element live {width,height} to the named state key (wireMeasure).

ref.reason: Publishes the element's live DOM node under ref.<name> in the mount-scoped RefRegistry and withdraws it on unmount (wireRef); consumers resolve it over the bus.

settle.reason: Root-only readiness: settle="manual" defers screen.ready until dsx.screen.settled() (kernel screen.ts + dom router).

enter.reason: Universal motion attr mirroring Stack.swift (StackEntry/visibilityBody/StackStyle): CSS opacity/transform. The curve NUMBERS come from the shared UI motion kernel (@despia-native/kernel parseMotion, corpus OpenSource/Conformance/motion/) — the web no longer carries its own table. Two named approximations: slide-* is a 16px offset+fade standing in for native .move(edge:), and anim="spring" is the kernel spring SAMPLED into a CSS linear() easing (CSS has no spring primitive) — both recorded in the module header and architecture/proposals/ui-motion.md.

exit.reason: Root-only dismiss animation is a FRAME concern: the router owns unmount and its config-plane motion lane (packages/dom/src/motion.ts) is the natural home. Deferred there rather than faked per-element; enter= covers appear.

dynamicType.reason: Polyfilled onto the ROOT RAMP. Native scales a fixed point size with the OS text-size setting (@ScaledMetric on iOS, scale-aware .sp on Compose); a browser exposes no per-element hook into that ramp, but `rem` IS the ramp, since the root font size is what browser text scaling moves. `fontSize` under `dynamicType="true"` compiles to calc(<n> / 16 * 1rem), which turns a global mechanism into the per-element opt-in the attribute promises. At the default 16px root the computed value is the SAME pixel count, so nothing moves for a reader who never changed the setting; at a 24px root a 17pt label becomes 25.5px while an un-opted-in one stays 17px. Both directions are asserted by the type-attributes oracle probe.

dynamicTypeMax.reason: The cap on the dynamicType ramp, as min(calc(<n> / 16 * 1rem), <cap>px) - the same 'cap the SCALED size' semantic iOS applies and Compose converts back to sp. Falls out of the same fontSize case.

Accordion.reason: The global Web twin provides accessible disclosure semantics, reactive title/open state, toggle events, and the named header slot that REPLACES the default title + chevron.
knownLimits: Expand/collapse animates grid-template-rows over --dsx-dur-base and collapses instantly under prefers-reduced-motion.
A custom header slot owns its own content entirely — the renderer contributes no chevron, exactly as the native slot replaces the default header view.

ChatBubble.reason: The global Web twin renders the directional bubble, bound value/children, semantic colors, and bounded width.
knownLimits: Web uses the neutral DSX token skin rather than cloning a native messaging bubble.

Checkbox.reason: The global Web twin uses a real checkbox input with bound state, label, change write-back, and keyboard/focus semantics.
knownLimits: The check glyph is CSS-drawn rather than an SF Symbol.

DSXView.reason: The rich Web twin mounts the screen component src names from this build's compiled registry (the web reading of the native rule that a shipped tag of the same name always wins), with reactive src re-resolution, the stable dsx-view lifecycle events, and a labelled unavailable state.
knownLimits: src resolves against the compiled component registry only: remote DSX fetching, screen-folder manifests, and the native DSXRemoteCache/offline generation policy are native-only, so origin is not consumed.
An unresolvable src renders the labelled dsx-view-unavailable status card instead of the native retryable DSXNativeUnavailable screen.
DSXView.fallback: Mounts the dsx-view host and resolves src from the compiled registry; a src this build does not ship renders a labelled role=status unavailable card, never blank and never a fake native surface.

DSXWebView.reason: The rich Web twin mounts the composed app web surface as the same policy-constrained iframe WebView rides, resolving path against this page's own origin (an explicit origin wins) with the shared lifecycle events and the named-surface controls the Dom facet targets.
knownLimits: No BridgeKit bridge is faked: the embedded page gets the plain window.app.send channel and the bridge-gate on:denied event never fires on Web.
The screen-readiness hostedSurface gate stays native-only: a web frame does not defer settled to the embedded page's first paint.
Browser sandbox and storage behavior cannot duplicate the native composed-surface WKWebView process/data-store guarantees.
DSXWebView.fallback: Mounts the functional policy-constrained iframe at origin+path (defaulting to this page's own origin); bridge-dependent behavior is absent rather than imitated.

Drawer.reason: The application-control Web twin implements BOTH declared presentations: the modal drawer (adaptive geometry, focus containment and restoration, background inerting, Escape and scrim dismissal, bounded content, 120px drag dismissal) and, at the shared desktop step, the standing drawer pinned in flow (collapse-to-rail control, keyboard- and pointer-resizable drag hairline within min/max, honest complementary semantics, no scrim or focus trap).
knownLimits: Modal drag dismissal begins from a 44 by 44 pixel handle instead of the native whole-panel gesture surface, a deliberate accessible-target adaptation.
Web uses a neutral token-driven surface instead of cloning the native fixed dark treatment.
Drawer is full-application chrome and is deliberately rejected from self-contained custom-element embeds (nothing renders there rather than broken chrome).

LevelMeter.reason: The Studio audio level meter has no Web renderer or audio-analysis seam.
knownLimits: No visual-only placeholder is reported as functional metering.
LevelMeter.fallback: Mounts the honest dsx-unsupported placeholder — a labelled marker carrying the <LevelMeter> name and the dsx-unsupported class; never blank, never a fake lookalike of the native surface.

MenuBar.reason: The application-control Web twin implements bounded keyed items, canonical selection state and write-back, selection events, radio-menu semantics, keyboard and RTL navigation, the compact pill dock, and, at the shared desktop step, the WAI-ARIA menubar presentation: roving roots, per-root shadow-3 flyouts from nested items, submenu keyboard walk with Escape walking up, and right-aligned shortcut hints from the shortcut token grammar.
knownLimits: Icon names resolve through the shared cross-runtime table (OpenSource/Conformance/icons/sf-map.json), so every name that draws on iOS/Android also draws here; an SF name absent from that table still needs an icon-web= adapter.
Web uses neutral adaptive chrome rather than native Liquid Glass or Material component skins.
MenuBar is full-application chrome and is deliberately rejected from self-contained custom-element embeds (nothing renders there rather than broken chrome).

ProgressRing.reason: The global Web twin renders an accessible SVG progress ring with bound value/max, line width, colors, size, and label.
knownLimits: Animation timing follows Web motion preferences and is not a pixel clone of SwiftUI.

RadioGroup.reason: The global data-control twin renders real radio inputs from CSV or bound option data and writes the selected value back.
knownLimits: Options and labels are bounded by the shared data-control safety ceilings.

Scene360.reason: No panorama renderer is registered for Web.
knownLimits: A flat image is not claimed as interactive 360-degree scene support.
Scene360.fallback: Mounts the honest dsx-unsupported placeholder — a labelled marker carrying the <Scene360> name and the dsx-unsupported class; never blank, never a fake lookalike of the native surface.

Scene3D.reason: The RealityKit scene contract has no WebGL/WebGPU model renderer.
knownLimits: Model loading, camera, lighting, and lifecycle parity remain unimplemented.
Scene3D.fallback: Mounts the honest dsx-unsupported placeholder — a labelled marker carrying the <Scene3D> name and the dsx-unsupported class; never blank, never a fake lookalike of the native surface.

Signature.reason: The global Web twin is a real pointer-driven ink pad: a devicePixelRatio-scaled 2D canvas drawing the SHARED ink law (@despia-native/kernel signature-core: clamp, round-at-capture, midpoint quadratic curve), one bound write per stroke on pointer-up, and a server twin that renders the committed strokes as an inline SVG in the same normalized space, so a signed document has real first paint before the pad mounts.
knownLimits: A pointer-drawn pad has no keyboard or switch-control equivalent on any renderer; the element exposes role=img with an empty/signed label and the documented pattern pairs it with a typed-name field.
Stylus pressure and tilt are dropped: the wire shape carries one width per stroke, so the same value draws identically on the four renderers.

Skeleton.reason: The global Web twin renders a size/radius-aware loading placeholder hidden from assistive technology.
knownLimits: Shimmer is disabled by the shared reduced-motion rules.

knownLimits: Key, scale, and snap attributes are not consumed on Web.
StudioPitchEditor.fallback: Mounts the honest dsx-unsupported placeholder — a labelled marker carrying the <StudioPitchEditor> name and the dsx-unsupported class; never blank, never a fake lookalike of the native surface.

knownLimits: A static text label is not claimed as timecode parity.
StudioTimecode.fallback: Mounts the honest dsx-unsupported placeholder — a labelled marker carrying the <StudioTimecode> name and the dsx-unsupported class; never blank, never a fake lookalike of the native surface.

StudioTimeline.fallback: Mounts the honest dsx-unsupported placeholder — a labelled marker carrying the <StudioTimeline> name and the dsx-unsupported class; never blank, never a fake lookalike of the native surface.

knownLimits: Clip editing and transport synchronization remain native-only.
StudioTrim.fallback: Mounts the honest dsx-unsupported placeholder — a labelled marker carrying the <StudioTrim> name and the dsx-unsupported class; never blank, never a fake lookalike of the native surface.

Table.reason: The global Web twin renders the whole native Table contract: a semantic, scroll-contained table from bound rows, declared columns/fields (fields defaulting to the lowercased column labels), semantic tint, header cell traits and one combined accessibility element per row.
knownLimits: Rows, columns and cell text are bounded for hostile input; a truncated source stamps data-dsx-truncated and logs once, rather than reconciling an unbounded table.

Sorting, selection, editing, column resizing and virtualization are not part of the contract on ANY runtime — the native reference is a plain data table too. Compose <grid> with a row template when cells need custom controls.

Waveform.reason: The Studio waveform surface has no Web renderer.
knownLimits: Peak generation, selection, mute state, and deterministic seeded rendering are not implemented.
Waveform.fallback: Mounts the honest dsx-unsupported placeholder — a labelled marker carrying the <Waveform> name and the dsx-unsupported class; never blank, never a fake lookalike of the native surface.

WebView.reason: The rich Web twin provides a policy-constrained iframe, lifecycle events, named controls, safe URL schemes, and ephemeral isolation.
knownLimits: Script/call/set/css controls require same-origin access.
Browser sandbox and storage behavior cannot duplicate WKWebView process/data-store guarantees.
WebView.fallback: Mounts the functional policy-constrained iframe (lifecycle events, named controls, safe URL schemes, ephemeral isolation); cross-origin script controls are inert rather than throwing.

alert.reason: The overlay twin provides modal alert semantics, focus containment/restoration, bound presentation, normalized actions, and dismissal.
knownLimits: Web uses DSX modal chrome rather than a browser alert() or native alert skin.

audio.reason: The media Web twin implements the fixture's full transport/readout contract: headless HTMLMediaElement playback, reactive transport/scrubbing bindings, bounded ready/time/buffering/error events, a 15-second load deadline, teardown, feature-detected Media Session commands, and the session= playback/ambient category applied through the page-scoped Audio Session API where the engine has one.
knownLimits: session= maps to the page-scoped Audio Session API where available (reflected as data-dsx-session and applied while the element plays); native audio categories, mixing, and silent-switch behavior otherwise remain OS policy a browser cannot reproduce.
Media Session, codecs, autoplay, background playback, and remote controls remain browser/OS policy and are unavailable in some engines.

Audio is selectively available to self-contained embeds. The latest locked production-equivalent qualification measured 45142 bytes gzip for audio and 45186 bytes for combined audio/video, leaving 4990 bytes below its declared 50176-byte qualification budget; the default self-contained widget budget remains 40960 bytes, and a build-time test pins these figures. The last move: the pt-attribute plane went number-typed like the native parsers (cssmap ptOrNull/fitOrNull, width/height fit-content, grow=both honored), 26 bytes, plus 11 from the @despia-native scope rename riding the same qualification.

button.reason: The base Web twin renders real button/anchor semantics with label, icon, iconSize, bordered/prominent variants, destructive/cancel roles, href navigation, disabled gating, and tap/double-tap activation — the full button.json attribute contract.
knownLimits: Press feedback is neutral DSX motion rather than a pixel clone of the native 0.92 press-scale recognizer.

Icon names resolve through the shared cross-runtime sf-map corpus (OpenSource/Conformance/icons/sf-map.json): 89 rows draw a 24x24 stroke vector, the ten pictographic rows draw the corpus unicode fallback glyph, and an SF name absent from the corpus paints the fail-open placeholder plus one console warning (override with icon-web=).

calendar.reason: The data-control twin renders a localized, keyboard-operable month grid with ISO binding, range constraints, marks, and month events.
knownLimits: The visible surface is one month at a time and mark input is bounded.

carousel.reason: The structural twin renders accessible slides with two-way current-page binding, snap paging, selection dots, peek and spacing geometry, and change events — the full carousel.json attribute contract.
knownLimits: Slides are capped at the 1,000-child structural safety ceiling and are not virtualized.
Native peek physics are adapted to CSS scroll-snap rather than reproducing the UIKit paging recognizer.

chart.reason: The rich Web twin renders accessible SVG line, area, bar, and point charts from bound data.
knownLimits: Multi-series, stacking, legends, secondary axes, and animation options are not implemented.
interpolation=linear|smooth|monotone|step, color=, xGrid= and yGrid= are implemented on the single-series SVG.
More than 2,000 source points are deterministically downsampled.
chart.fallback: Mounts the functional accessible SVG chart (line/area/bar/point from bound data); unimplemented series/axis options are omitted, never a blank canvas.

canvas.reason: The <canvas> surface renders the shared display list into an HTML canvas, with the SSR SVG path byte-identical to the native twins. Tier-1 children, the paint set, transforms, gradients and the fill-rule fold all come from the shared CanvasCore, so a shape cannot mean one thing here and another on a phone.
knownLimits: Tier 2 is a declarative command list replayed through the kernel recorder, not a live Canvas2D context handle: the payload seam carries data, never a mutable graphics object.
on:frame is display-linked and installed only while bound, mounted and on screen, so an off-screen canvas costs nothing.

combobox.reason: The native-control twin implements an editable ARIA combobox/listbox with filtering, keyboard navigation, option binding, selection, and disabled state.
knownLimits: Options and label text are bounded for untrusted data.

confirmDialog.reason: The overlay twin provides an adaptive confirm dialog with modal semantics, normalized actions, focus containment/restoration, and dismissal.
knownLimits: Visual placement adapts to Web viewport/input rather than cloning platform dialog chrome.

contextmenu.reason: The overlay twin supports context-click and long-press opening, nested actions, roles, separators, keyboard traversal and focus restoration, on the same long-press timing the native gesture recognizer uses.
knownLimits: Touch long-press opens at 500 ms with a 10 px slop — a DECLARED match for UILongPressGestureRecognizer's default minimumPressDuration, which the native contextMenu rides; the constant is exported and pinned so a drift is a parity change, not a tweak.
Menu depth and item/text sizes are bounded for hostile input, and the platter is the renderer's own neutral surface rather than the OS blurred preview platter.

datepicker.reason: The native-control twin uses browser date/time controls with normalized DSX wire values, label, color, disabled state, and write-back.
knownLimits: Picker presentation and locale chrome are browser/OS controlled.

divider.reason: The base Web twin renders the semantic-token divider and accepts universal style/color overrides.
knownLimits: Hairline rasterization follows the browser device-pixel ratio.

field.reason: The form twin supplies labeled controls, shared form state, touched/dirty/error tracking, validation, secure inputs, and option fields.
knownLimits: Validation is synchronous and the custom pattern grammar is deliberately bounded.

flow.reason: The structural twin provides wrapping flow layout with bounded reactive item and line spacing.
knownLimits: Browser flex-wrap resolves fractional layout differences independently of SwiftUI.

form.reason: The form twin manages namespace state, child fields, validity, scrolling, and submit actions/events using a real form element.
knownLimits: Async/server validation orchestration remains application-owned.

grid.reason: The structural/binding twin renders semantic grid rows/cells with responsive columns, keyed reconciliation, spacing, scroll, and reach-end handling — the full grid.json attribute contract (bind/key/columns/spacing/scroll/reachEnd).
knownLimits: Bound grids reconcile at most 1,000 live rows per update (data-dsx-truncated is exposed) and are not virtualized; larger sources must be paged by the application.
CSS grid layout owns browser-specific fractional column rounding.

hstack.reason: The base Web twin renders a horizontal flex stack with DSX spacing/alignment through the universal style contract.
knownLimits: Flexbox rounding follows browser layout.

image.reason: The base Web twin renders remote and relative images, every icon name in the shared cross-runtime sf-map corpus, the fixture's decorative-by-default accessibility contract, iconSize/fontSize geometry, semantic tint and the cache policy.
knownLimits: A NATIVE app-bundle asset key (asset="AppLogo") has no browser equivalent — a browser has no app bundle. A path or URL asset resolves normally; a bare key stamps data-dsx-unresolved="asset" and keeps its accessible name, so the gap is inspectable rather than a silent blank box.
cache="none" is expressed as a per-mount cache-bust key; the default rides the browser's own HTTP memory/disk cache, which is the platform's equivalent of the native image cache tier.

The web icon tier is generated from OpenSource/Conformance/icons/sf-map.json and covers all 99 corpus rows; 89 draw a 24x24 stroke vector and 10 pictographic rows (apple.logo, bitcoinsign.circle.fill, books.vertical, crown.fill, flame.fill, metronome, pianokeys, target, tuningfork, waveform.badge.magnifyingglass) deliberately draw the corpus's own unicode fallback glyph instead.

Thirteen names the in-repo web previews author live in the corpus web_extra section rather than icons, because an icons row also pins a Material Symbols codepoint that the bundled Android subset font must carry.

lightbox.reason: The media Web twin provides a shared-top-layer modal gallery with bounded safe sources, reactive presentation/index, focus containment/restoration, keyboard and RTL paging, pointer swipe, interactive drag dismissal, responsive controls, and deterministic SSR.
knownLimits: Native pinch zoom, double-tap zoom, and pan-while-zoomed are not implemented; browser page pinch zoom remains available.
Image decoding/caching follows browser policy and the normalized gallery is capped at 256 entries.

Lightbox is full-application-only because it requires shared host-level portal/inert ownership and its locked slice exceeds both the default 40960-byte widget budget and the 50176-byte media qualification ceiling.
lightbox.fallback: Mounts the functional top-layer gallery (modal presentation, keyboard/RTL paging, pointer swipe and drag dismissal); native pinch/double-tap zoom is absent while browser pinch-zoom remains.

list.reason: The structural/binding twin implements the whole fixture contract: semantic rows, keyed identity, write-back scope, spacing/axis/scroll/alignment, reach-end, group_by sections in first-seen order, the swipe-action rails with both firing shapes and per-edge full-swipe commit, drag reorder that writes the moved array back through the bind seam and fires on:move with FINAL indices, and the horizontal autoscroll marquee — under the same construct gating List.swift uses (scroll="false" and a horizontal axis win over all three; a grouped list ignores reorder; an active reorder suppresses swipe) and with an SSR twin that paints the same first frame.
knownLimits: Bound lists render at most 1,000 live rows and are not virtualized — an explicit allocation ceiling rather than a missing behavior, reported on the element as data-dsx-truncated / total-count / rendered-count.
A swipe rail is bounded at 8 buttons per edge and 120 characters per label/icon/colour token, the same containment the overlay item model applies to authored data.

Swipe buttons are real focusable buttons that a rail opens on focus, rather than DOM hidden until a gesture: the web/AT-honest twin of the native rotor actions, at the cost of extra tab stops per row.

Drag reorder and the marquee frame loop are inherently interactive, so the server paints the handle and the closed rails statically and the client wires the pointer drag, the keyboard ArrowUp/ArrowDown move and the animation on mount.

Reorder needs a plain dotted bind path to write the moved array back through; a computed bind expression has no write seam, so the handles do not appear at all rather than moving a row nothing records.

The autoscroll marquee loops by rotating the leading row to the end instead of cloning a second track (a duplicate would fork keyed row identity); it pauses under pointer/focus and stands down entirely under prefers-reduced-motion.

lottie.reason: No built-in Lottie player ships with the runtime; <lottie> is a MODULE element, and the Core/Lottie web facet (the vendored lottie-web light player, MIT, pinned) fills the tag through the module component loader whenever the module is registered.
knownLimits: With Core/Lottie registered the facet consumes src (a Lottie .json URL, absolute or site-relative), loop, speed, autoplay, a11yLabel and on:finish; loading and failure render labelled states inside the element's own box, and prefers-reduced-motion pins the static first frame.
The module facet renders via SVG only and plays plain Lottie JSON: dotLottie (.lottie) archives, bundled-name lookup, and expression-driven animations are not supported on this surface.
Without the module (excluded builds, sliced embeds), src, loop, speed, and autoplay are not consumed.
lottie.fallback: Mounts the honest dsx-unsupported placeholder whenever the Core/Lottie module is absent — a labelled marker carrying the <lottie> name and the dsx-unsupported class; never blank, never a fake lookalike of the native surface.

rive.reason: No Rive runtime ships with the web renderer; <rive> is a MODULE element, and the Core/Rive web facet fills the tag through the module component loader whenever the module is registered and its pinned @rive-app/canvas player was fetched by the build.
knownLimits: With Core/Rive registered the facet consumes src, artboard, stateMachine, animation, inputs, autoplay, fit, alignment, speed, ref, a11yLabel and the on:load / on:stateChange / on:event / on:error handlers; the input fold, the selection refusals, fit and alignment and the playback schedule all come from the shared kernel core, so a state machine cannot mean one thing here and another on a phone.

The player is 2.2 MB of js and wasm and is fetched in CI from the coordinate pinned in the module's dsx.lock.json. A build without that fetch reports the typed absence (unsupported_platform) and renders the labelled unavailable card, never blank pixels.
Without the module (excluded builds, sliced embeds), no attribute is consumed.
rive.fallback: Mounts the honest dsx-unsupported placeholder whenever the Core/Rive module is absent - a labelled marker carrying the <rive> name and the dsx-unsupported class; never blank, never a fake lookalike of the native surface.

map.reason: The rich Web twin provides an offline coordinate plane with accessible pins and pointer/keyboard pan/zoom.
knownLimits: It does not render map tiles, routes, regions, circles, user location, or the native map style/glyph contract.
It is a coordinate visualization, not a geocoding/navigation SDK.
map.fallback: Mounts the functional offline coordinate plane (accessible pins, pointer/keyboard pan/zoom); tiles/routes/regions are absent, never a broken map-SDK surface.

menu.reason: The overlay twin provides anchored nested menus with normalized actions, roles, separators, focus management, and keyboard traversal.
knownLimits: Menu item/depth/text input is bounded and placement adapts to the viewport.

otp.reason: The native-control twin implements a segmented one-time-code input with binding, paste/input normalization, completion event, and accessibility labeling.
knownLimits: Length and displayed value are capped by explicit safety limits.

pager.reason: The structural/binding twin renders horizontal/vertical snap paging with two-way current-page binding, keyed bound pages, selection dots, and change events — the full pager.json attribute contract.
knownLimits: Bound pages are capped at the 1,000-page structural safety ceiling and are not virtualized.
Scroll-boundary commit follows browser scroll events rather than reproducing the native ~80 ms vertical-commit implementation detail.

picker.reason: The native-control twin uses a real select control with static/bound options, labels, disabled state, and value write-back.
knownLimits: Presentation and menu chrome are browser/OS controlled; options are bounded.

popover.reason: The overlay twin provides an anchored, viewport-aware popover with trigger semantics, dismissal, keyboard handling, and focus restoration.
knownLimits: Arrow preference may flip/clamp to remain visible and browser layout controls subpixel placement.

pressable.reason: The base Web twin provides whole-area button/anchor semantics with child content and universal tap, double-tap, long-press, and navigation wiring.
knownLimits: Gesture recognition uses PointerEvent/browser timing rather than native recognizer internals.

progress.reason: The base Web twin provides an accessible determinate progressbar with clamped bound value and semantic track/fill styling.
knownLimits: The Web control is DSX-drawn rather than the platform's native progress component.

qrcode.reason: The rich Web twin generates deterministic SVG QR matrices with size, colors, correction level, accessible labeling, and fail-closed input handling.
knownLimits: Oversized or invalid payloads render an explicit unavailable status instead of an approximate code.

rangeslider.reason: The native-control twin implements two bounded range inputs with normalized low/high constraints, throttled write-back, final commit, and accessible labels.
knownLimits: Overlapping-thumb visuals and pointer arbitration follow the browser implementation.

refreshable.reason: The data-control twin implements the fixture's on:refresh/busy contract: scroll-contained content, rubber-band pull on touch and fine pointers with the shared overscroll curve, a built-in always-visible 44px refresh control for keyboard and mouse with hover and focus-visible states, a polite live status region, aria-busy reflection, spin progress with reduced-motion collapse, and busy-gated completion.
knownLimits: Completion is driven by the bound busy state (350ms grace without one) inside start/maximum safety windows rather than a native refresh-control lifecycle; a refresh that never settles is finished by the safety timeout and announced in the status region.
The pull gesture arms only while the viewport is scrolled to the top and contains its own overscroll; any browser or OS page-level pull-to-refresh chrome stays the platform's own.

scaffold.reason: The base Web twin provides an accessible adaptive split/stack shell with sidebar/content/inspector panes, authored widths, collapse policy, and labels.
knownLimits: Web uses semantic CSS layout and does not claim NavigationSplitView, WinUI, or GTK chrome.

scroll.reason: The base Web twin provides vertical or horizontal overflow layout and renders child content through the common binding/style contract.
knownLimits: Scrollbar appearance and momentum are browser/OS controlled.

searchbar.reason: The Web twin is the composite search field the native reference draws: a leading magnifier, the real search input with binding, the Search placeholder default and submit, and a trailing clear button that writes the bound path back and fires on:clear.
knownLimits: The leading and trailing glyphs are drawn as control chrome rather than resolved through the shared icon corpus, so a control affordance can never depend on an icon name being present in that table.
The browser's own type=search cancel affordance is suppressed in favour of the declared clear button, and its `search` event is routed through the same on:clear contract.

segmented.reason: The rich Web twin provides an accessible radiogroup with static/bound options, selection write-back, and arrow/Home/End keyboard behavior.
knownLimits: Chrome is neutral DSX Web styling rather than a cloned native segmented control.

segmentedButton.reason: The data-control twin implements single or multiple segmented selection, labels/icons, binding, keyboard traversal, and accessibility state.
knownLimits: Option and icon lists are bounded and normalized.

sheet.reason: The overlay twin implements modal sheet/inset/full modes, normalized detents, title/close/action chrome, focus containment/restoration, and dismissal.
knownLimits: Detents and drag behavior adapt to browser viewport/input rather than reproducing native sheet physics.

slider.reason: The base Web twin uses a real range input with binding, min/max, input write-back, and semantic tint styling.
knownLimits: Track/thumb geometry and input cadence are browser controlled rather than UISlider internals.

spacer.reason: The base Web twin participates as flexible space in DSX stack layout and accepts universal size constraints.
knownLimits: Flex distribution uses CSS layout rounding.

spinner.reason: The base Web twin provides an accessible status spinner with semantic color/scale styling and reduced-motion handling.
knownLimits: It is DSX CSS-rendered rather than a browser-native progress indicator; authored scale is bounded to 0.25x through 4x to contain hostile remote markup.

split.reason: The structural twin provides the two/three-pane plan (paneRole resolution, collapseAt/expandAt width classes), the phone stack push with a back pop, the overlay sidebar, ARIA window-splitter dividers with drag and keyboard resize, and value/on:change detail routing.
knownLimits: Presentation resolves from the split's own container width (ResizeObserver) rather than a native split host; the platform Back chrome is a kernel-rendered button.

stack.reason: The base Web twin provides the generic DSX flex/display container and universal spacing/alignment/style contract.
knownLimits: CSS flex/grid layout owns browser-specific fractional rounding.

stars.reason: The rich Web twin renders fractional SVG star fills with read-only or radiogroup semantics, binding, and keyboard selection.
knownLimits: Count and size are bounded to protect DOM and layout.

stepper.reason: The base Web twin provides the visible label caption, named decrement/value/increment controls, semantic tint, fixture-default bounds, bound numeric updates and press-and-hold acceleration.
knownLimits: Press-and-hold repeat is pointer driven (500 ms hold, then repeats accelerating from 240 ms to a 60 ms floor); a held keyboard Enter uses the platform's own key repeat and deliberately does not double-step.
The caption element only exists when label= is authored, so an unlabelled stepper keeps the bare minus/value/plus anatomy the native control shows.

svg.reason: The media Web twin implements the fixture's full asset/src/d/viewBox/fill/width/height contract over the same static shape/path subset the native renderer draws (rect/circle/ellipse/line/polygon/polyline/path with M L H V C S Q T Z absolute and relative), with semantic paint tokens, decorative-by-default accessibility, deterministic SSR, and fail-closed canonicalizing sanitization.
knownLimits: A NATIVE app-bundle resource name (asset="logo", or src naming a bundled file) has no browser equivalent because a browser has no app bundle; the twin stays network-free by design, stamps data-dsx-unresolved="asset"|"src" (the image precedent) and renders nothing, so the gap is inspectable rather than a silent blank.

Scripts, styles, references, images, groups, animation, unknown attributes, and oversized documents fail closed. Inline SVG root width/height above 16384px are rejected, DSX host width/height are clamped to 16384px, and shape coordinates are independently bounded to an absolute value of 1000000000.
SVG is full-application-only because its locked slice exceeds both the default 40960-byte widget budget and the 50176-byte media qualification ceiling.

tabs.reason: The structural twin provides ARIA tabs/tabpanels, bound selection, icons/badges/titles, change events, and keyboard traversal.
knownLimits: Tab chrome and overflow behavior adapt to DSX Web rather than a native tab bar.

text.reason: The base Web twin renders bound/value/inner content with semantic color and universal typography, the inline markdown vocabulary the native reference renders, and lineLimit tail truncation.
knownLimits: markdown= implements the INLINE vocabulary Text(AttributedString(markdown:)) renders on the reference runtime — emphasis, strong emphasis, code, strikethrough and links. Block constructs (headings, lists, quotes) stay their literal run of text on every runtime, exactly as SwiftUI's Text collapses them.

A markdown link target is restricted to http/https/mailto/tel and relative URLs; any other scheme renders as plain text rather than a live navigation, and the parse is bounded to 16384 characters, 512 inline nodes and 8 levels of nesting.
lineLimit uses the browser line-clamp box, so the ellipsis and the exact break position are engine-owned typography rather than a pinned glyph count.

textarea.reason: The base Web twin uses a real textarea with binding, placeholder, input, focus and blur events, and grows between minLines and maxLines exactly like the native lineLimit(min...max) contract.
knownLimits: Auto-grow counts hard line breaks and the CSS cap bounds soft-wrapped lines, so the maxLines ceiling is enforced by box height rather than by a per-glyph wrap measurement.
Line counts are bounded to 1..64 and a reversed minLines/maxLines pair normalizes by swapping, never by trapping — the twin of the native input policy.
The user-drag resize handle is a browser affordance the native control has no equivalent for; it is left in place rather than suppressed.

textfield.reason: The base Web twin uses a real text/password input with binding, placeholder, change, submit, focus and blur events, and maps the fixture's contentType/keyboard tokens onto autocomplete/inputmode/type.
knownLimits: keyboard= sets inputmode (and, for email/phone/url, the matching input type); a numeric keyboard deliberately stays type=text so the field keeps its literal value instead of a locale-parsed number.
An unrecognized contentType/keyboard token leaves the platform default in place, exactly as an unknown UITextContentType does on the native runtime.
Which autofill entries a browser actually offers is user-agent and profile owned; the renderer declares the field's meaning, it cannot force the suggestion.

toggle.reason: The base Web twin uses a real checkbox input with switch semantics, bound state, change write-back, and accessible focus handling.
knownLimits: Track/thumb chrome is a web-only iOS-26-ish capsule polyfill (63x28, pill thumb), glass-free and token-overridable (--dsx-toggle-*, color=). It is not a hosted UISwitch or Material switch; iOS and Android keep the platform control.

toolbar.reason: The structural twin provides toolbar semantics, position/spacing, child content, and roving arrow/Home/End focus behavior.
knownLimits: Material/backdrop rendering follows browser support and forced-colors fallbacks.

video.reason: The media Web twin implements the fixture's full contract: native HTML video rendering, active-page ownership, reactive transport/scrubbing/readout bindings, subtitles, bounded load/error state, accurate isolated target-frame previews, best-effort Media Session commands, the audio= playback/ambient category via the page-scoped Audio Session API where present, accessibility, and deterministic SSR.
knownLimits: audio= maps to the page-scoped Audio Session API where available (reflected as data-dsx-session and applied while the element plays); automatic background Picture-in-Picture is not promised and pip only feature-gates browser PiP availability.

Target-frame preview requires the media to be canvas-readable (same-origin, blob, or CORS-enabled) and fails closed otherwise; codec, autoplay, subtitles, background playback, and Media Session behavior vary by browser/OS.

Video is selectively available to self-contained embeds. The latest locked production-equivalent qualification measured 45144 bytes gzip for video and 45186 bytes for combined audio/video, leaving 4990 bytes below its declared 50176-byte qualification budget; the default self-contained widget budget remains 40960 bytes, and a build-time test pins these figures. The last move: the pt-attribute plane went number-typed like the native parsers (cssmap ptOrNull/fitOrNull, width/height fit-content, grow=both honored), 26 bytes, plus 11 from the @despia-native scope rename riding the same qualification.

vstack.reason: The base Web twin renders a vertical flex stack with DSX spacing/alignment and slot content through the universal style contract.
knownLimits: Flexbox rounding follows browser layout.

wheelpicker.reason: The native-control twin provides an always-visible select list with static/bound options, label, disabled state, and value write-back.
knownLimits: It does not reproduce inertial wheel physics, snapping, or native haptics; selection chrome is browser controlled.
wheelpicker.fallback: Mounts the functional always-visible select list (static/bound options, label, disabled, write-back); inertial wheel physics and haptics are absent, never a blank picker.

zstack.reason: The base Web twin provides layered stack layout and DSX alignment through the universal style contract.
knownLimits: Stacking and intrinsic sizing follow CSS layout rules.

Panorama.reason: The alias has no Web factory because the canonical panorama surface is unsupported.
knownLimits: Renders the explicit unsupported fallback.
Panorama.fallback: Resolves to the honest dsx-unsupported placeholder because the canonical <Scene360> surface is native-only on Web; the marker names the tag and is never blank.

Model3D.reason: The alias has no Web factory because the canonical 3D scene surface is unsupported.
knownLimits: Renders the explicit unsupported fallback.
Model3D.fallback: Resolves to the honest dsx-unsupported placeholder because the canonical <Scene3D> surface is native-only on Web; the marker names the tag and is never blank.

Scene3DView.reason: The alias has no Web factory because the canonical 3D scene surface is unsupported.
knownLimits: Renders the explicit unsupported fallback.
Scene3DView.fallback: Resolves to the honest dsx-unsupported placeholder because the canonical <Scene3D> surface is native-only on Web; the marker names the tag and is never blank.

glassButton.reason: The alias resolves to the fully functional button Web twin (label, icon, variants, roles, href navigation, activation).
knownLimits: Web renders a neutral DSX variant rather than native Liquid Glass chrome.

transport.reason: The alias resolves to the fully functional button Web twin (icon, activation, role, navigation, accessibility).
knownLimits: Web renders neutral DSX transport chrome rather than a media-platform-specific native button skin.

date.reason: The alias resolves to the datepicker native-control twin.
knownLimits: Browser/OS controls own presentation.

row.reason: The alias resolves to the functional arbitrary-content pressable twin with tap, double-tap, long-press, and navigation behavior.
knownLimits: Gesture recognition uses PointerEvent/browser timing rather than native recognizer internals.

capsuleProgress.reason: The alias resolves to the accessible determinate progress twin with canonical six-pixel geometry and semantic tint tracking.
knownLimits: The Web control is DSX-drawn rather than the platform's native progress component.

refresh.reason: The alias resolves to the supported refreshable Web twin and inherits its contract and limits.
knownLimits: Inherits the refreshable twin's busy-gated completion and top-of-scroll pull arming.

activity.reason: The alias resolves to the accessible spinner Web twin.
knownLimits: The visual is DSX CSS-rendered.

tabview.reason: The alias resolves to the full structural tabs Web twin.
knownLimits: Web tab chrome is platform-adaptive.

label.reason: The alias resolves to the text Web twin and inherits its full contract, including markdown and lineLimit.
knownLimits: It renders a <label> element and does not infer a target control association; the native alias is plain text, so there is no association to mirror.
Every text= limit applies verbatim — the inline markdown vocabulary and the engine-owned line-clamp break position.

input.reason: The alias resolves to the textfield Web twin and inherits its full contract, including the contentType/keyboard mapping.
knownLimits: Every textfield limit applies verbatim — an unknown token leaves the platform default, and browser autofill behavior stays user-agent owned.

switch.reason: The alias resolves to the real checkbox input with switch semantics.
knownLimits: The visual is neutral DSX Web chrome.

_fallbackNote: Every non-supported row (partial or unsupported) additionally carries a machine-readable `fallback`: the deliberate degraded UX the DOM renderer shows in place of the missing behavior — the functional twin for a partial row, the labelled dsx-unsupported placeholder for an unsupported one. packages/dom/test/element-support-ledger.test.ts requires it AND renders it, so a future silent gap (a non-supported row with no declared, honest fallback) fails the gate.
_webClassNote: Every row declares `webClass`: the stable `.dsx-*` class the Web renderer stamps on that element's ROOT (/web/17 — the class contract application CSS targets). It is not prose: packages/dom/test/element-support-ledger.test.ts renders each tag through the DOM-free @despia-native/server string renderer and fails when the declared class is not the class actually emitted, so a renaming refactor cannot silently break an application stylesheet. An `unsupported` row declares `dsx-unsupported` — the labelled placeholder the DOM renderer mounts (a capitalized native-only tag emits NOTHING server-side, because SSR cannot know whether a module facet will provide it, and the client mounts the marker). Folding this same column into the GENERATED editor catalog (OpenSource/Documentation/reference/stack-elements.json) needs its Ruby generator, ClosedSource/scripts/generate_editor_catalog.rb — a different lane.
